tiers.text: The back window's latch is rotten through. Someone has painted over it twice rather than replace it.

variants.text: The rotten latch is one thing. The fence panel on the east side is another: wired on, not bolted. It would lift.

tiers.text: There's a back window that might give with enough force. May not be quiet, though.

variants.text: A fire escape runs up the depot's side wall, rust-brown and loose at the bottom rung. The back window might give as well.

physics.miss: Brick, shutters, a bolted gate. Nothing that moves.

tiers.text: One guard is flagging, eyes half shut. His flask is empty and he keeps checking it anyway.
One guard keeps shifting his weight, the way a man does at the end of a double shift.

life.miss: Four coats and a lot of breath. You can't tell who's awake.

tiers.text: The nearest guard is jumpy. He flinches at his own radio. Easy to rattle.
One guard keeps glancing at the door, then at his phone, then at the door.

emotion.miss: Flat faces, arms folded. They've done this before.

tiers.text: The patrol has a gap. You count it twice. Forty seconds, every round, like a bus timetable.

variants.text: The patrol gap is forty seconds. The camera over the door sweeps on a slower beat, and you count that too.

tiers.text: The rounds run roughly on the quarter hour. Roughly.

time.miss: You can't make out any shift or predictable patrol routes.

tiers.text: You catch the moment one guard will turn away. A second before he does it.

variants.text: You catch the moment one guard will turn away. And the camera over the door has a flicker in it, waiting to go.

tiers.text: Something is about to go wrong for someone here. Not necessarily you.

fate.miss: No chances you can see here. It's just a yard at night.

cards.label: {today} — The approach
cards.text: Nobody has put a sign on this vein, but the ground still belongs to someone. You case the approach twice. No obvious watchers. That's not the same as no watchers.
A fenced yard, a guard hut, a depot door. Three ways to start.
